citations.narrative:
The facility representative withheld from APHIS officials that she was performing scent gland removal surgeries on skunk
kits during a routine unannounced inspection and falsely attributed the surgeries to her attending veterinarian.
APHIS officials asked the facility representative how the scent glands were being removed in skunk kits prior to sale of the
animals, and the facility representative stated that her veterinarian was performing the scent gland removal procedure.
APHIS Officials inquired if the facility could provide any medical records or receipts from the veterinarian to which the
representative stated that she did not have any records or documentation available. APHIS Officials attempted to contact
the attending veterinarian by phone several times. The attending veterinarian left a voicemail on 21-October-2026 stating
he did teach the facility how to remove the scent gland in skunk kits 2 years ago and he hoped that was ok. APHIS
Officials were unable to speak with the attending veterinarian directly regarding the facility but were able to speak with the
veterinary clinic office manager, who confirmed that the facility has not brought any skunk kits into the clinic to have
surgical procedures performed by a veterinarian. When speaking with the facility representative again on 27-October-
2026 the representative admitted she has been removing the scent glands from skunk kits herself at the facility.
Providing false information about who has been conducting surgeries on the regulated animals interfered with APHIS
officials’ ability to evaluate compliance with the Animal Welfare Act and to ensure the well-being of the animals.
A licensee shall not interfere with, threaten, abuse (including verbally abuse), or harass any APHIS official in the course of
carrying out his or her duties.
Correct from 27-October-2026 and going forward.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The licensee failed to follow the AV’s requirement for annual visits, according to the Program of Veterinary Care. When
APHIS Officials inquired when the attending veterinarian last visited the premises, the facility representative stated the
veterinarian visited in June. The facility representative could not provide any documentation confirming the recent visit to
the premises. When speaking with the office manager of the veterinary clinic regarding the annual site visit, the individual
confirmed that a site visit has not been conducted at this facility since June 2025.
Without the required regularly scheduled visits to the premises, the AV was not given the opportunity to ensure the
provision of adequate veterinary care. The lack of annual visits as directed within the Program of Veterinary Care can
create serious health and well-being issues in the animals.
Each dealer and exhibitor shall employ an attending veterinarian under formal arrangements. In the case of a part-time
attending veterinarian or consultant arrangements, the formal arrangements shall include a written program of veterinary
care and regularly scheduled visits to the premises of the dealer or exhibitor.
Correct by 27-November- 2026

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility is not providing appropriate veterinary care and methods to remove the scent glands in young skunk kits.
Young skunks are having their scent glands removed by the licensee without general anesthesia, according to the
attending veterinarian. Years ago, the attending veterinarian had previously provided verbal and in-person instruction for
the licensee to remove the scent glands from skunk kits herself at the facility, with an assistant to restrain the animals.
When inquiring with the licensee on 27-October-2026 on how she performs the procedure the facility representative
stated that she has an assistant restrain the skunk with the hind-end pointing towards the ground and after the skunk
"sprays" they are taken to a table and placed on it's back. Pressure is applied to the rectal area and the glands are
exposed allowing removal by hemostatic forceps. APHIS Officials inquired on if any pain medication is provided to the
animals and the representative stated that a gel is rubbed on the anal region but could not provide the name of the
product.
Scent gland removal is a major surgical procedure which produces permanent impairment of physical and physiological
function, as defined by the Animal Welfare Act Regulations and Standards, with a high risk for complications such as
rectal prolapse. With this major surgical procedure being performed on conscious animals with the ability to move and
squirm, the risk of complications is inherently increased. The procedure being performed by the licensee does not provide
adequate veterinary care and can lead to unnecessary pain and distress to the animals.
The facility shall establish and maintain a program of adequate veterinary care that includes appropriate methods to
prevent, control, diagnose and treat the animals on hand by having surgical procedures performed by a knowledgeable
veterinarian.
Correct from this day forward Oct 27, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
